source_title: Kempsey's water supply now entirely reliant on rainfall
evidence_description: Reports that, amid severe drought, Willawarrin was already receiving trucked water (approx. 17,000 litres) because iron and manganese levels in the stressed Macleay River had exceeded the Australian Drinking Water Guidelines, and that Bellbrook was expected to need trucked water within a week. Describes the Macleay River as near standstill (preventing bore recharge), Steuart McIntyre Dam at approximately 80% and falling, an estimated 1,900 ML of remaining supply (about 15 months without rain), and Level 2 water restrictions in place, with Level 3 anticipated if the dam fell below 70%.
relevant_quotation: This is our last remaining water supply.
investigation_relevance: Earliest evidence located of the drought-driven water crisis that led to the 2019-2020 trucked-water period for both Willawarrin and Bellbrook; establishes the drought/river-extraction context behind the iron and manganese contamination.

source_title: Willawarrin and Bellbrook return to river supply after months of trucked-in water (media release)
evidence_description: Official council media release confirming Willawarrin and Bellbrook were switched back to river water supply on Thursday 18 June 2020, ending several months of trucked-in water. States the cause as naturally occurring iron and manganese reaching unsafe levels in the Macleay River due to the combined effects of drought, bushfire, and subsequent heavy rainfall causing soil erosion, creating potential health risk plus taste and laundry-staining complaints. States the fix was a combination of bore water and treatment processes.
relevant_quotation: There's a real sense of achievement to have Willawarrin and Bellbrook back on river
investigation_relevance: Primary/official record of the resolution of the 2019-2020 trucked-water episode; anchors the end date of that episode and the stated cause and interim fix, directly relevant to Historical failures, Trucked water, Iron contamination, and Manganese contamination.

source_title: Willawarrin and Bellbrook return to river supply after months of trucked-in water
evidence_description: Independent media report corroborating EV-0002's facts (same restoration date, same cause, same Wes Trotter quote), consistent with both being drawn from the same underlying council media release. Also republished in substantially the same form by Port Macquarie News (SRC-0004).
investigation_relevance: Independent corroboration of the primary council record (EV-0002) that Willawarrin and Bellbrook's trucked-water period ended on 18 June 2020.

source_title: Willawarrin's new water treatment plant construction set for 2025
evidence_description: Reports that LC Water was awarded the design-and-construction contract for a new Willawarrin water treatment plant, with detailed design expected to finish early 2025 and construction to follow. States the existing treatment system was built in 1967 and required repeated water carting during droughts, bushfires, and floods. Gives an original 2024 cost projection of approximately $4 million, noted as since revised (see EV-0005/EV-0006 for the $8 million figure). Funding cited as NSW Safe and Secure Water Program ($2m+) and Kempsey Shire Council ($6m+). Quotes then-Mayor Leo Hauville and a named NSW Department official.
relevant_quotation: built way back in 1967 and is in desperate need of an upgrade
investigation_relevance: Names the contractor (LC Water) and the original, lower cost projection for the Willawarrin plant, and gives the specific 1967 construction date of the existing infrastructure; both the contractor identity and the cost revision have not yet been independently confirmed against a primary council record.

source_title: $52.9m locked-in for landmark water infrastructure project
evidence_description: Official NSW Government announcement of a $52.9 million regional water infrastructure package: $12.5m from the Australian Government's National Water Grid Fund, $13.2m from the NSW Government's Safe and Secure Water Program, and $27.1m from Kempsey Shire Council. Primarily funds a new filtration plant treating raw water from the Steuart McIntyre Dam (2,500 ML capacity, built after the 1994 drought) and the Sherwood Borefield, serving over 18,000 residents across Kempsey, Frederickton, Smithtown, and Gladstone, with construction starting mid-2025 over an 18-month program. States this package 'builds on' the separate, already-announced $8 million Willawarrin plant ($2m NSW Government + $6m Council), serving the village's 130 residents. Quotes federal Minister Tanya Plibersek, NSW Minister Rose Jackson, and Kempsey Shire Council Mayor Kinne Ring.
relevant_quotation: this new plant will be a game changer
investigation_relevance: Identifies the Willawarrin plant's funding as one component of a larger $52.9m regional water security program, and reveals a much larger parallel project (Steuart McIntyre Dam/Sherwood Borefield) for the main Kempsey network; also documents Mayor Kinne Ring in office by this date.

source_title: Sod turns on new $8 million Willawarrin water treatment plant
evidence_description: Official NSW Government release marking the start of construction (sod-turning) on the $8 million Willawarrin water treatment plant ($2m+ NSW Government, $6m+ Kempsey Shire Council), replacing the existing 1960s-era infrastructure. States Willawarrin (population 180 per this release) relies on bore water that becomes unsuitable during extreme weather, requiring water carting from Kempsey. Describes the new plant as a 0.25 ML/day ultrafiltration plant with UV disinfection, water storage, reticulation pumps, and chemical dosing, located south of the town's sports field; pipelines already installed; reservoir refurbishment to follow commissioning. States the project is expected to finish by early 2026. Quotes NSW Minister for Water Rose Jackson and Kempsey Shire Council Mayor Kinne Ring, who refers to consultation with the community since 2018 and cites severe weather events between 2017 and 2022 as the impetus.
relevant_quotation: I have firsthand knowledge of how unreliable the current water supply is
investigation_relevance: Primary/official record establishing the construction start date, technical scope, funding split, and expected completion window for the Willawarrin plant - the central document for the Treatment Plant and Construction threads.

source_title: Kempsey Shire moves to Level 2 water restrictions
evidence_description: Reports Kempsey Shire Council moving to Level 2 water restrictions due to minimal forecast rainfall and declining Macleay River flow, on which the Sherwood Borefield depends. Lists Willawarrin and Bellbrook among the water supply schemes affected, alongside Kempsey/Lower Macleay, South West Rocks, Hat Head, Crescent Head, and Stuarts Point. Notes Steuart McIntyre Dam's water quality had recently improved and could become a future supply source. Warns Level 3 restrictions were likely if dry weather continued.
relevant_quotation: we need to take immediate steps to conserve water locally
investigation_relevance: Earliest evidence found so far of the drought conditions that led to the 2019-2020 trucked-water episode - five months before EV-0001 (Oct 2019) - and confirms both Willawarrin and Bellbrook were already affected by June 2019.

source_title: Kempsey Tap Water Passes Safety, Below PFAS Limits
evidence_description: Reports Kempsey Shire Council PFAS testing (October-December 2024) across eight water supply systems - Kempsey, Lower Macleay, Crescent Head, Hat Head, South West Rocks, Stuarts Point, Willawarrin, Bellbrook, and Thunggutti Aboriginal Community - all showing undetectable levels of PFOA, PFOS, PFHxS, and PFBS, well within applicable guideline limits.
relevant_quotation: the results showed undetectable levels of key PFAS substances
investigation_relevance: First Bellbrook-specific evidence located since the 2020 restoration (EV-0002/EV-0003): confirms Bellbrook was an actively monitored, operating supply system as of late 2024 and passed PFAS testing, though it does not address Bellbrook's treatment infrastructure or upgrade status (contaminant tested is PFAS, not the iron/manganese this case centres on) - Q-0002 remains open.
